fit.gap_handling_summary: The documents generally distinguish academic backend work, freelance work and the short internship honestly. They do not manufacture two years of professional experience, end-to-end testing, WCAG compliance, Docker or health-data expertise. The strongest bridges are accessibility testing, the Node.js/PostgreSQL project, the yoga site and teaching assistance. However, the application does not directly explain the seniority shortfall or articulate a specific learning approach to health-data privacy, and its current student framing is unreliable.

issues: No email address, telephone number or other contact route is supplied. These were not provided in the source material, so they should be requested rather than invented.
The spring 2025 teaching-assistant role appears after the May–August 2024 internship.
Current 'Third-year student' status is carried over from an earlier letter despite a final-year project dated 2024–2025. Education status and dates need confirmation.
Education gives neither attendance dates nor a confirmed qualification/status beyond the stale year description.
PostgreSQL storage of favourites is repeated in adjacent Tidewatch bullets.
The language entry 'English' does not communicate proficiency.
No project or portfolio URL is supplied. The ad welcomes one, but no URL was available to reuse.

reasons: The PDF extracts in a sensible single-column order with intact words and conventional headings.
Core React, TypeScript, Node.js and PostgreSQL terms are prominent.
SQL is supported by PostgreSQL work but is not stated explicitly in the CV; semantic screening may still recognise it.
The stated four-month internship and project-led profile do not meet a strict two-year professional-experience screen.
Several screening terms, especially Git, end-to-end testing, security and privacy, are absent because the supplied material does not establish them.
Missing contact details reduce application usability even though they do not prevent text extraction.

stale_framing: I am a third-year Computing student
issues: The opening repeats historical third-year status without confirming that it remains current.
The long second paragraph reads largely as a compressed CV and tool inventory.
The opening places React and TypeScript experience alongside the internship in a way that could imply TypeScript internship experience; only React is documented for that employment.
Privacy by default is mentioned as an attraction, but the letter does not explicitly express willingness to learn health-data privacy requirements.
The candidate's unusually relevant personal reason for caring about screen-reader accessibility is omitted.
It does not directly position this as an application from someone below the advertised professional-experience threshold.
strengths: Names Verdane Care, the Full-Stack Engineer role and the Patient Experience team.
Uses the company's patient focus, accessibility commitment and privacy-by-default principle accurately.
Supports its main technical statements with concrete projects and the internship gallery.
Includes the teaching-assistant experience as credible evidence of supporting others without claiming engineering leadership.
Does not misrepresent the yoga site as regulated clinical software or the academic backend as professional backend employment.
Polite, readable and contained on one page.

spacing_issues: The hackathon entry is split across the CV page break, leaving 'Developed the frontend.' as an isolated continuation bullet at the top of page two.
The CV's second page is only 42.2% filled, while page one is comparatively dense. Shortening repetition and lower-priority material could improve balance or enable a tighter junior CV.
The standalone 'English' entry occupies a full additional-information section for very little useful content.
issues: Both documents use a coherent serif style, readable 11-point body text and safe margins.
The CV has clear section rules, bold entry labels and right-aligned dates, but page-break control needs improvement.
The cover letter has a conventional, readable block layout with no visible clipping or overlap.

fluency_and_tone_issues: 'These projects have given me experience across frontend development, APIs, SQL data, and Jest and React Testing Library.' mixes development domains and individual tools in an awkward list.
'hands-on academic, freelance, and hackathon experience building React and TypeScript interfaces' compresses several different contexts and makes the scope of each technology less clear.
The letter's extended project-and-technology paragraph is fluent but repetitive and less personal than the available source material permits.

parsed.summary: The documents present the candidate's strongest genuine assets well: React/TypeScript projects, practical screen-reader testing, an accessibility internship, a wellness site and teaching assistance. They mostly preserve the distinction between project experience and professional employment, but incorrectly carry historical third-year student framing into the current application. The CV lacks contact details, reverses the order of its experience entries and has an awkward page-break continuation. The cover letter is accurately targeted to Verdane Care but too inventory-heavy, and the application remains unlikely to pass a strict two-year professional-experience screen.
